page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-intel is a virtual private server belonging to the High Performance family. It is configured with an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor featuring 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model. The system includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and is bundled with 100 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this server in the lower tiers of performance. In stress-ng testing, the single-core CPU performance scored 1391.28, and the multi-core score reached 2729.87, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth tests show a significant drop-off from cached small-block reads at 190.16 GB/sec to uncached large-block reads at 11.67 GB/sec and writes at 9.16 GB/sec, which are categorized in the bottom 10%. Geekbench results reflect similar constraints, with a single-core score of 982.0 and a multi-core score of 1733.0.

Given its shared CPU architecture and modest memory capacity, this server offers a highly cost-efficient entry point for lightweight workloads that do not require sustained high-performance compute resources. It is suitable for basic web serving, small-scale Redis caching, development environments, and lightweight background tasks. However, it is not recommended for memory-intensive databases, large-scale software compilation, or machine learning inference, as demonstrated by its low LLM prompt processing speed of 133.52 tokens/second on a small 135M model.
